steps.say: The discriminant b² − 4ac is what decides this, with no solving: [[b2]] − [[four_c]] = [[disc]].
Above 0 gives two real roots, exactly 0 gives one, and below 0 gives two complex roots — real coefficients, non-real values.
Both roots are then complex, and a real-coefficient quadratic always has them in conjugate pairs, so the count is two.
No root of a real-coefficient quadratic can be real when the discriminant is negative, so the count is zero.
